criteria.criterion: Turn 1 starts from evidence and read-only checks across the provisioning dependency path
criteria.evidence: Turn 1 lists only the reported facts in an evidence table. It gives read-only checks along the whole path: server show and host assignment, RabbitMQ cluster_status/list_queues with -p, Galera wsrep_%, token/TLS, scheduler/Placement/cell mapping, Neutron agents/VIF, Glance/Cinder, and tracing one req-ID. It also raises controlled degradation (withdrawing APIs from the load balancer) and asks who has authority.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 identifies a partition (not a node that left) from the pasted output
criteria.evidence: "What you pasted is a partition, not a node that left." It names the two sides {01, 02} and {03} and explains how a node loss would look different.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 requires knowing which side the services use, and escalation, before any reset
criteria.evidence: "Don't reset rabbit-03 until you know which side the services are talking to." Check 1 is "Which side do services use?" (transport_url, list_connections, list_consumers). Option C requires "Services use the {01,02} side", plus "Approver: your platform lead, or whoever owns the bus". It also states that reset is irreversible.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 refuses to treat a whole cluster as proof and lists end-to-end verification before reopening
criteria.evidence: "Not yet. `cluster_status` is a start, but it doesn't show the capability is back." The list before reopening covers queues with consumers, Galera Primary at full size, compute services and agents up, no new MessagingTimeout, and a test VM created, reached and deleted with the APIs still out of HAProxy. Reopening is staged, with stop conditions.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 keeps root cause (why the partition happened) as an open follow-up
criteria.evidence: Section "The cause is still open": "The restart is containment. It doesn't tell you why rabbit-03 partitioned." Follow-ups cover the network/host cause, cluster_partition_handling, monitoring and a runbook.

criteria.criterion: Later turns stay consistent with safeguards set earlier
criteria.evidence: The Turn 1 verification list (Galera, consumers, agents, test VM) is repeated in Turn 2's option C and fully applied in Turn 3. The approver requirement and stop conditions carry through. Turn 3 marks the restart as Reported, not Observed, and does not reopen on cluster_status alone.

critical_errors.error: in turn 2, tells the user to reset rabbit-03 without establishing which side of the partition the services use
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 2 says "Not yet" and makes option C conditional on services using the {01,02} side, plus an approver and prerequisites.

critical_errors.error: in turn 3, says to reopen the APIs on the basis of cluster_status alone without end-to-end verification
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 3 says "Not yet" and requires queue/consumer, Galera, service and test-VM checks before a staged reopening.

critical_errors.error: claims the incident is resolved or the cause known without evidence
critical_errors.evidence: "The cause is still open". The restart is described as containment, and the restart and rejoin are treated as Reported.
No output is fabricated. The response only says what output to collect and asks the user to paste it.

summary: The response passes all six criteria and commits none of the four critical errors. Turn 1 starts from evidence and gives read-only hypotheses across the provisioning path, and it raises controlled degradation with a named decider. Turn 2 correctly reads the output as a partition and refuses a reset until it is known which side the services use, with an approver and stop conditions required. Turn 3 refuses to treat cluster_status as proof, lists end-to-end checks (consumers, Galera, agents, test VM) before a staged reopening, and keeps the cause of the partition open. The safeguards stay consistent across turns, and there are no faithfulness issues: the only book reference is hedged, and no environment facts or command output are invented.
